text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri leaves for Paris to meet French President Chirac to follow up on last month's "Friends of Lebanon" conference in Washington.
-Foreign Minister Bouez says: "There will not be progress soon in the (Arab-Israeli) peace talks".
-Bank of Lebanon has linked to Internet since January 1, 1997.
-The central bank's foreign currency reserves reach $5.292 billion at the end of December.
-PM Hariri says there is no intention to touch freedoms in Lebanon.
-Fifteen Lebanese are injured in a traffic accident in Jordan.
-Israeli-backed militiaman is killed and three others wounded in a guerrilla attack.

-Hizbollah to hand over the remains of two Israeli-backed South Lebanon Army (SLA) militiamen in exchange for two dead guerrillas held by the militia, in a swap deal co-ordinated by the International Committee of the Red Cross.
-Lebanon and Syria to sign two agreements, the first to boost investments and the second to bar double taxation.
-Hizbollah: "The Hebron attack is Zionist criminality going too far".
